candidate.answerReason: The derivative \(2x-4\) changes from negative to positive at \(x=2\), establishing a local minimum there. Completing the square independently confirms the same coordinate.

methods.label: Derivative sign test
methods.explanation: \(f'(x)=2x-4=0\), so \(x=2\). The derivative is negative to the left and positive to the right, so this is a local minimum point.
methods.levelReason: Polynomial differentiation and the first-derivative sign test fit the stated elective mathematics volume.

methods.label: Completing the square
methods.explanation:
Completing the square exposes the vertex:
\[
f(x)=x^2-4x+1=(x-2)^2-3.
\]
For every real \(x\), \((x-2)^2\ge0\), with equality only at \(x=2\). Hence the vertex \((2,-3)\) is a minimum point and therefore also a local minimum point. The requested \(x\)-coordinate is \(2\).
methods.levelReason: Vertex form and nonnegativity of a square provide a distinct argument using earlier algebra.
